theme: The LORD reigns; he is robed in majesty
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 93. It is a short psalm that announces the reign of the LORD and speaks of him as mightier than the floods. Read it as a brief hymn that opens a series of enthronement psalms (93, 95-99).
settingTheScene: Psalm 93 has no author, but it is one of the “The LORD reigns” psalms. It was probably sung in worship celebrating God’s kingship, perhaps at a festival. In the ancient world, floods and seas represented chaos and the forces that threaten order. This psalm declares that the LORD is mightier than all of them. It helps us read Revelation, in which seas, beasts, and floods seem to threaten the people of God, but in which the throne is secure.
observation: “The LORD reigns; he is robed in majesty” (v. 1).
“He has put on strength as his belt” (v. 1).
“Yes, the world is established; it shall never be moved” (v. 1).
“Your throne is established from of old; you are from everlasting” (v. 2).
“The floods have lifted up their voice” (v. 3).
“Mightier than the thunders of many waters, mightier than the waves of the sea, the LORD on high is mighty!” (v. 4).
“Holiness befits your house, O LORD, forevermore” (v. 5).
interpretation:
The psalm opens with a proclamation: “The LORD reigns; he is robed in majesty; the LORD is robed; he has put on strength as his belt.” The Hebrew word for “reigns” can also be rendered “has become king,” and the psalm was probably sung to celebrate God’s kingship. He is clothed like a king in majesty and strength. “Yes, the world is established; it shall never be moved.” Because God is king, the world is stable. The world is not a random accident but is held in place by his rule.

Next, the eternity of his throne: “Your throne is established from of old; you are from everlasting.” Before the world existed, God reigned. His throne is not a recent achievement. This is why the elders in Revelation 4 praise the one who was and is and is to come.

Then the threat: “The floods have lifted up, O LORD, the floods have lifted up their voice; the floods lift up their roaring.” Three times, the floods are mentioned, building like waves. They represent every power that threatens: chaotic nature, hostile nations, and demonic forces. The floods are loud, and the repeated phrasing suggests that they will not stop. But the next verse puts them in perspective: “Mightier than the thunders of many waters, mightier than the waves of the sea, the LORD on high is mighty!” The floods roar, but God is mightier. His voice, in Psalm 29, is heard over the waters.

The psalm ends with two statements about God’s word and house. “Your decrees are very trustworthy; holiness befits your house, O LORD, forevermore.” His commands can be trusted, and his dwelling place is holy. The God who rules the floods is also the God who speaks reliably and calls his people to holiness.

For Christians, the picture is complete in Jesus, who stilled the storm with a word (Mark 4:39), walked on the waves, and calmed the seas that frightened his disciples. They said in awe, “Who then is this, that even wind and sea obey him?” This psalm is the answer. And in Revelation, the Lamb stands on the throne above the chaos, and the sea of glass before the throne is calm (4:6). In the new creation, “the sea was no more” (21:1): the symbol of chaos is gone.
connection: Psalm 29:3, 10 also pictures God enthroned over the flood. Psalm 95-99 are other enthronement psalms. Exodus 15:18 declares that the LORD will reign forever. Mark 4:35-41 shows Jesus calming the storm. Job 38:8-11 shows God setting limits for the sea. Psalm 65:7 and 89:9 speak of stilling the waves. Isaiah 43:2 promises that waters will not overwhelm. Revelation 4:6, 15:2, and 21:1 mention the sea. Revelation 11:15 and 19:6 announce that God reigns. Hebrews 12:28 speaks of receiving an unshakable kingdom.
application:
When you feel like the floods are lifting up their voice (anxiety, news, conflict), say verse 4 aloud.

Thank God for the stability of his rule. Name three things in your life that rest on it.

Pray that your church’s life would reflect the holiness that befits his house.
prayerPrompts: Praise God as king, robed in majesty.
Thank him that the world is established and cannot be moved.
Tell him what you are holding that you want him to uphold.
